reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but implements daily skipping and holiday classification separately in the server consumers.

duplication.why: Daily-skip policy is repeated across shared and server code, the two handlers duplicate filtering and adjustment pipelines, and forward/reverse enumeration repeats filtering.

placement.why: Handler registration belongs in the server app, but daily skipping and holiday interpretation belong alongside the existing shared scheduling rules.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested scheduling features, their configuration plumbing, and related tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several implementations of the same scheduling policy, including separate holiday representations and unexplained enumeration limits.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts classify nonworking days locally and disable applyWeekendRule for daily schedules instead of sharing the complete scheduling decision.

disguised_duplication.where: The server handlers express shared/schedules.ts's isNonWorkingDay decision as inline date-fns and holidays.includes predicates, reshaping rather than sharing the policy.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains holidays; getNextDate adds two daily-specific filtering branches, applyWeekendRule adds explicit after/before dispatch branches, and both server date handlers independently implement daily skipping and holiday classification.
